button_map: LP1=Tekken 1=Left Punch, RP2=Tekken 2=Right Punch, LK3=Tekken 3=Left Kick, RK4=Tekken 4=Right Kick
what_this_is: RESCOPED 2026-10-24 per coordinator reconciliation update: Additive T7 overlay dataset under game/assets/movesets/t7/ (+ game/assets/anim/t7/). It does NOT edit any existing moveset file: no file is rewritten, so there is zero clobber surface. Each overlay file is keyed by Tekken fighter slug + notation_lp + row context (notes/stance) — notation_lp ALONE is not unique in the source data (duplicate notations exist for stance/context variants; the validator counts them per fighter). This INDEX maps every WH moveset file to its overlay slug(s). The inline-merge step (writing t7 blocks into the 157 files themselves) is a follow-up merge once the combat lane confirms this schema — see 'deviation' in the PR body. SHIP RULE (user 2026-10-24 20:22 CDT, supersedes narrower framings): WH ships with NO famous names + proprietary canon names. Tekken fighter slugs/names in this directory are TECHNICAL source identifiers only (the same rule as Tekken names in technical files, never in canon writing) — they are not shipped roster names and this PR never ships the original game itself. We USE the owned files to wire OUR OWN game; we do not supply or redistribute full games. SOURCE HIERARCHY (same directive): work must be 100% from the files, from the FULL GAME FILES where available — owned full files are authoritative, not community approximations. That is why the frv/dnc mot.bin tables (from the owned T7 files, MERGED PR #61) outrank community frame rows for ANIMATION mapping, while FRAME data here remains community-sourced (TheBigTuna / TekkenDocs) until full-file frame extraction lands via GPU Job 1's mot.bin batch. SCOPE OF THIS PR: T7 coverage for fighters OTHER than the 8 T7-mapped fighters (+torch) in PR #1039's scope, DLC frame data (9 chars), T7 anim banks/lookup maps, per-character patterns, 29 UNMAPPED stances, and the 188 canon MADE moves — all of which the coordinator update explicitly keeps in this lane.

errata_source_artifacts_preserved_verbat.notation_lp_bare_digits: 7 rows across 4 fighters still carry bare digits in notation_lp after the prior lane's conversion, preserved verbatim here (not silently fixed): lidia 8 rows with stance tag 'CF0' (a stance label, not a button — legitimate, do not 'fix' by deleting the stance); ling 1 row 'f, F+RK4, When guarded4' (source note leaked into the notation string); steve 5 rows with '12~' shorthand (e.g. 'f+12~RP2' — the 1,2 buttons written without '+' in the source); yoshimitsu 1 row 'f, F+RP2 Hit in front1+RP2' (source note leaked into the notation string). The inline-merge lane must normalize the steve/ling/yoshimitsu artifacts (with a documented mapping, never by deleting rows) before engine use, and must never treat those rows as validated LP1/RP2/LK3/RK4 rows. The validator (validate-t7-overlay.mjs) lists every such row.
errata_source_artifacts_preserved_verbat.duplicate_notations: Most fighters contain duplicate notation_lp values (same input, different rows — stance/context variants, e.g. 'WS+LP1' twice, 'f+LK3' twice). These are source-faithful, NOT deduped here: the prior lane removed only EXACT duplicate rows. Any consumer joining on notation alone will collide; join on notation_lp + notes/stance context, or take the first row and flag the collision. Per-fighter duplicate counts are printed by the validator.
errata_source_artifacts_preserved_verbat.string_prefix_rows: Most T7 strings do NOT have every proper prefix as a standalone row (King: 53 of 77 strings lack at least one prefix row). That is normal frame-data shape (full strings listed, continuations not always standalone) — it is NOT a missing-data error, but the engine must never fall back from a missing prefix row to a chord row. See the validator's string checks.

name_join.status: PENDING — 0 of 6,909 overlay moves carry a wavu.wiki name in this PR. name is null on every move.
name_join.why_not_joined_here: TheBigTuna source carries notation only (its own files warn: 'NO move names in source'). WH files' own t7 blocks also carry no names (ids like king_2 only; display names like 'PANTERA 1 (T3 king r110)' are generated placeholders, NOT move names, and were deliberately NOT copied as names). A wavu.wiki T7 page was text-fetched for King (https://wavu.wiki/t/King_movelist_(Tekken_7)) and it IS real T7 data with names — but its text rendering flattens tables so row order (name vs input vs stats) cannot be resolved reliably from the fetch alone (e.g. whether 'Palm Strike' names input 1 or 1,2). Joining names off flattened text would invent attributions, which the exactness rule forbids.
name_join.method_for_the_join_lane: For each of the 45 overlay fighters: fetch that fighter's wavu.wiki T7 movelist page (same /t/<Name>_movelist_(Tekken_7) pattern as King, verified per fighter, never guessed in bulk), parse the WIKI TABLE STRUCTURE (not flattened text) so Name/Input/Hit level/Damage columns stay aligned, join to overlay rows on normalized notation ONLY (never on damage — wavu sheet damage differs from TheBigTuna MOD damage, e.g. King LP1: wavu 7 vs MOD 9), and report join rate per fighter. Unmatched rows keep name=null. Alternative join source already in-repo: the 52 mot.bin JSONs from GPU Job 1 carry T7 internal move names (e.g. frv/dnc 'name' fields) — those are internal ids, not display names, and must not be presented as wavu names without a mapping table.
